instrument: EU AI Act (Regulation (EU) 2024/1689, as amended by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744)
requirement_in_plain_words: Who is provider and who is deployer is settled and recorded, and re-checked whenever the system is renamed, substantially modified or put to another purpose
how_met_and_what_remains: The responsibility matrix allocates each duty to provider or deployer; the classification assessment is completed and signed in the application for each deployment (OA-01); the Article 25 check is repeated when the system is renamed, substantially modified or put to another purpose

instrument: EU AI Act (Regulation (EU) 2024/1689, as amended by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744)
requirement_in_plain_words: People operating or using the system need sufficient AI literacy
how_met_and_what_remains: Training is recorded per person in the application and anyone working on matters without a current record is reported by the routine checks (OA-03); the training itself is the organisation's

instrument: EU AI Act (Regulation (EU) 2024/1689, as amended by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744)
requirement_in_plain_words: Classification follows intended purpose; use to assist a judicial authority or similarly in ADR is listed as high-risk
how_met_and_what_remains: Each profile carries a regulatory note in every report; the classification assessment for the deployment is completed and signed in the application (OA-01)

instrument: EU AI Act (Regulation (EU) 2024/1689, as amended by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744)
requirement_in_plain_words: The system complies with the requirements of Chapter III, Section 2, taking into account its intended purpose and the state of the art
how_met_and_what_remains: Each Section 2 requirement (Arts. 9-15) has its own row and controls; confirming compliance as a whole is the conformity assessment (OA-11)

instrument: EU AI Act (Regulation (EU) 2024/1689, as amended by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744)
requirement_in_plain_words: A risk-management system kept live across the lifecycle
how_met_and_what_remains: Risk register is tied to controls and tests and checked by CI; a named person reviews it in the application every 90 days (OA-04)

instrument: EU AI Act (Regulation (EU) 2024/1689, as amended by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744)
requirement_in_plain_words: Data governance. Applies chiefly to training, validation and testing data; this system trains no model
how_met_and_what_remains: The same discipline is applied to what the system reads: sources are approved, versioned and status-dated; originals are hash-addressed; the provider states the data governance in the application (OA-21)

instrument: EU AI Act (Regulation (EU) 2024/1689, as amended by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744)
requirement_in_plain_words: Technical documentation drawn up before placing on the market and kept up to date
how_met_and_what_remains: The application generates the Annex IV technical documentation from the system's own records (controls, risks, requirements, workflow, models, evaluation, monitoring); the provider completes what only it can state and signs it off (OA-05)

instrument: EU AI Act (Regulation (EU) 2024/1689, as amended by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744)
requirement_in_plain_words: Automatic recording of events over the system's lifetime, enabling traceability
how_met_and_what_remains: Every step, check set, hold, decision and release is logged in a tamper-evident chain and reconciled per run

instrument: EU AI Act (Regulation (EU) 2024/1689, as amended by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744)
requirement_in_plain_words: Transparent enough for deployers to interpret output; accompanied by instructions for use
how_met_and_what_remains: Every report opens with a plain summary and states its limits and what was and was not verified; the desktop application shows each agent's mandate, each finding's checks and each hold's reason with what can be done about it; instructions for use are provided and the provider records that they were adapted and issued (OA-06)

instrument: EU AI Act (Regulation (EU) 2024/1689, as amended by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744)
requirement_in_plain_words: Effective human oversight: understand limits, detect problems, disregard or override, stop
how_met_and_what_remains: Named reviewer, visible held findings, acknowledged limits, override with separate permission, stop and controlled restart

instrument: EU AI Act (Regulation (EU) 2024/1689, as amended by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744)
requirement_in_plain_words: Appropriate accuracy, robustness and cybersecurity, with declared metrics
how_met_and_what_remains: A built-in evaluation prepares a matter with known defects planted in it and measures what was caught against thresholds the provider declares (OA-07); accuracy on representative real matters must still be measured by the provider before reliance

instrument: EU AI Act (Regulation (EU) 2024/1689, as amended by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744)
requirement_in_plain_words: Provider obligations and a quality management system
how_met_and_what_remains: Registers, change-assessment and incident forms support a QMS; where the QMS is documented and who runs it is recorded in the application (OA-08)

instrument: EU AI Act (Regulation (EU) 2024/1689, as amended by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744)
requirement_in_plain_words: Technical documentation, quality management documentation and the declaration of conformity are kept for ten years after the system is placed on the market
how_met_and_what_remains: Evidence packs and the ledger are kept for as long as the retention settings say; keeping the provider's documentation for ten years is the provider's (OA-09)

instrument: EU AI Act (Regulation (EU) 2024/1689, as amended by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744)
requirement_in_plain_words: Automatically generated logs are kept for an appropriate period (at least six months for deployers)
how_met_and_what_remains: Closing a matter keeps the ledger and decision records; retention periods are set in the application, the audit trail cannot be set below six months, and the routine checks delete closed matters' content when its period ends (OA-09)

instrument: EU AI Act (Regulation (EU) 2024/1689, as amended by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744)
requirement_in_plain_words: Corrective action when the system is not in conformity: bring it into conformity, withdraw, disable or recall it, and inform those concerned
how_met_and_what_remains: Runs can be stopped and restarted only by a named decision; incidents are opened automatically; informing deployers, distributors and authorities is the provider's (OA-15)

instrument: EU AI Act (Regulation (EU) 2024/1689, as amended by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744)
requirement_in_plain_words: Cooperation with competent authorities: information, documentation and logs provided on request
how_met_and_what_remains: Logs and evidence packs can be exported for any run; responding to an authority is the provider's (OA-15)

instrument: EU AI Act (Regulation (EU) 2024/1689, as amended by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744)
requirement_in_plain_words: A provider established outside the Union appoints an authorised representative in the Union
how_met_and_what_remains: Applies only if the provider is established outside the Union; whether it does, and who, is recorded in the application (OA-19)

instrument: EU AI Act (Regulation (EU) 2024/1689, as amended by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744)
requirement_in_plain_words: Importers and distributors verify the system's conformity before making it available
how_met_and_what_remains: Applies only where the system reaches the deployer through an importer or distributor; recorded in the application (OA-19)

instrument: EU AI Act (Regulation (EU) 2024/1689, as amended by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744)
requirement_in_plain_words: Use according to instructions; assign competent human oversight; monitor; keep logs
how_met_and_what_remains: The software requires a named reviewer whose role on the matter lets them approve, records training per person and provides monitoring; competence, supervision and time are the deployer's (OA-03, OA-10)

instrument: EU AI Act (Regulation (EU) 2024/1689, as amended by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744)
requirement_in_plain_words: Fundamental rights impact assessment, where the deployer is of a kind the Article covers
how_met_and_what_remains: Whether it applies depends on the deployer; the impact assessment is completed and signed in the application (OA-02)

instrument: EU AI Act (Regulation (EU) 2024/1689, as amended by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744)
requirement_in_plain_words: Conformity assessment based on internal control before the system is placed on the market or put into service
how_met_and_what_remains: Not performed by the software. The evidence pack, registers and generated technical documentation are its inputs; the application shows which organisation actions remain before it can be recorded (OA-11)

instrument: EU AI Act (Regulation (EU) 2024/1689, as amended by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744)
requirement_in_plain_words: An EU declaration of conformity is drawn up and the CE marking affixed
how_met_and_what_remains: The application drafts the declaration from the system's records (OA-12); completing, signing and affixing the marking are the provider's

instrument: EU AI Act (Regulation (EU) 2024/1689, as amended by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744)
requirement_in_plain_words: Registration in the EU database before the system is placed on the market or put into service (and, for deployers that are public authorities, registration of the use)
how_met_and_what_remains: The registration number is recorded in the application (OA-13)

instrument: EU AI Act (Regulation (EU) 2024/1689, as amended by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744)
requirement_in_plain_words: Transparency duties for certain AI systems, where relevant
how_met_and_what_remains: Model-drafted content is labelled as such in every report; telling the people affected is the deployer's (OA-14)

instrument: EU AI Act (Regulation (EU) 2024/1689, as amended by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744)
requirement_in_plain_words: Post-market monitoring; reporting of serious incidents
how_met_and_what_remains: Monitoring and incident records exist; a serious incident shows its Art. 73 reporting deadline; whether an incident is reportable, and reporting it, are human decisions (OA-15)

instrument: GDPR (Regulation (EU) 2016/679)
requirement_in_plain_words: Minimisation, storage limitation, integrity and confidentiality, accountability
how_met_and_what_remains: Logs hold identifiers not content; content is deleted when a closed matter's retention ends; observers and auditors see personal contact details masked; the lawful basis is the controller's (OA-09, OA-20)

instrument: GDPR (Regulation (EU) 2016/679)
requirement_in_plain_words: No decision based solely on automated processing with legal effect
how_met_and_what_remains: The system produces no decision; a named person decides everything

instrument: GDPR (Regulation (EU) 2016/679)
requirement_in_plain_words: Data protection by design and by default
how_met_and_what_remains: Local processing, network denied by default, matter isolation, minimal logs, and material withheld from anyone on a matter whose role does not include it

instrument: GDPR (Regulation (EU) 2016/679)
requirement_in_plain_words: Security appropriate to the risk
how_met_and_what_remains: Access control with proven identity, lock-out and a second factor, roles on each matter with clearance for its material, isolation, egress control, tamper evidence and an encrypted, hardened server are implemented; encryption at rest, backup, patching and network controls must come from the deployment (OA-16)

instrument: GDPR (Regulation (EU) 2016/679)
requirement_in_plain_words: Records of processing; data protection impact assessment
how_met_and_what_remains: The impact assessment is completed in the application (OA-02); the lawful basis and records of processing are recorded there (OA-20); the evidence pack supports both

instrument: National law implementing the GDPR (the use case takes Ireland's Data Protection Act 2018 as its local example)
requirement_in_plain_words: National rules that complete the GDPR: criminal-offence data, restrictions on data-subject rights in legal proceedings, privilege, supervision of courts acting judicially
how_met_and_what_remains: For the deploying organisation in its own member state; the software holds no national rule; the assessment is recorded in the application (OA-17)

requirement_in_plain_words: AI risk assessment and treatment
how_met_and_what_remains: Risk register maps each risk to controls with tests; reviewed in the application every 90 days (OA-04)

requirement_in_plain_words: AI system impact assessment
how_met_and_what_remains: Completed and signed in the application with the impact assessment (OA-02)

requirement_in_plain_words: Documented information controlled and available
how_met_and_what_remains: Registers, decisions and per-run evidence are versioned and hashed; the technical documentation is generated and signed off in the application (OA-05)

requirement_in_plain_words: Operational planning and control
how_met_and_what_remains: One versioned workflow definition and policy; both recorded on every run

requirement_in_plain_words: Monitoring, measurement, analysis and evaluation
how_met_and_what_remains: Monitoring snapshot, routine checks and the built-in evaluation; the periodic review is recorded in the application (OA-18)

requirement_in_plain_words: Nonconformity and corrective action
how_met_and_what_remains: Hold, incident, named resolution, controlled restart

requirement_in_plain_words: The AI system life cycle is controlled: requirements, design, verification and validation, deployment, operation and monitoring, technical documentation
how_met_and_what_remains: Requirements are tied to controls and tests and checked on every commit; workflow, policy, model and prompt versions are recorded per run and a change is flagged for assessment; the built-in evaluation measures what is caught (OA-07); each change is assessed in the application before use (OA-22); validation on real matters remains

requirement_in_plain_words: AI system recording of event logs
how_met_and_what_remains: See AIA-12

requirement_in_plain_words: Quality of data and data provenance
how_met_and_what_remains: Source versions, retrieval and status dates, hash-addressed originals

requirement_in_plain_words: Information for interested parties
how_met_and_what_remains: Every report opens with a plain summary and states its limits; instructions for use are recorded as issued (OA-06)

requirement_in_plain_words: The system is used according to its intended use
how_met_and_what_remains: Profiles fix who may use it and what it may say; prohibited actions are refused

requirement_in_plain_words: Responsibilities allocated between the organisation, its partners and suppliers
how_met_and_what_remains: See provider_deployer_matrix.csv; who is provider and deployer is recorded with the classification (OA-01); the agreement itself is between the parties

instrument: EU AI Act (Regulation (EU) 2024/1689, as amended by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744)
requirement_in_plain_words: No prohibited practice: nothing scores, profiles or predicts the behaviour of a person, assesses whether someone is likely to offend, or recognises emotions
how_met_and_what_remains: Nothing in the system assesses a person: facts are taken word for word with where they are, and no output rates credibility, character or the likelihood of offending; that it is not put to such a use is the deployer's to confirm (OA-23)

instrument: EU AI Act (Regulation (EU) 2024/1689, as amended by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744)
requirement_in_plain_words: The high-risk system meets the accessibility requirements of the Web Accessibility and European Accessibility Directives
how_met_and_what_remains: Keyboard use, enlarging every page, plain words and explanations on hover are built and tested; no audit against EN 301 549 (WCAG 2.1 AA) has been made and screen readers have not been tried (OA-24)

instrument: EU AI Act (Regulation (EU) 2024/1689, as amended by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744)
requirement_in_plain_words: A person affected by a decision taken on the basis of the system's output, with legal effect on them, can obtain a clear explanation of the part the system played and of the main elements of the decision
how_met_and_what_remains: Every run's evidence pack shows what the system read, the sources and models it used, what it checked and who approved what; giving the explanation, and the main elements of the decision, is the decision-maker's (OA-25)

instrument: Cyber Resilience Act (Regulation (EU) 2024/2847)
requirement_in_plain_words: An actively exploited vulnerability, or a severe incident affecting the product's security, is notified through the single reporting platform to the coordinating CSIRT and ENISA: an early warning within 24 hours, a notification within 72 hours, and a final report within 14 days of a fix being available (a vulnerability) or within one month (an incident); users are told what to do
how_met_and_what_remains: Nothing of this is in the software; who watches for exploitation, who decides and who reports are recorded in the application (OA-26)

instrument: Cyber Resilience Act (Regulation (EU) 2024/2847)
requirement_in_plain_words: Designed, made and supported to the essential cybersecurity requirements: vulnerabilities handled and fixed with security updates through a stated support period, a bill of materials, technical documentation, conformity assessment, declaration and CE marking
how_met_and_what_remains: Network refused by default, matter isolation and a tamper-evident ledger are built and tested, and a list of third-party components and their licences is made at each build (not yet a machine-readable bill of materials); the vulnerability process, support period, documentation and conformity assessment are the provider's (OA-27)

instrument: Product Liability Directive (Directive (EU) 2024/2853)
reference: Arts. 2(1), 4(1) and 7 (products placed on the market after 9 December 2026)
requirement_in_plain_words: Software is a product: its manufacturer is liable without proof of fault for damage to a natural person caused by a defect, including one that an update brings or the lack of a security update leaves, while the software is in its control
how_met_and_what_remains: For the provider: product-liability cover and a stated support and security-update period (OA-27); the deployer's own professional liability is separate
